overview: A self-managing, icon-only screen-share control button for Zoom Video SDK sessions on iOS, built for in-app/ReplayKit broadcast screen sharing. On tap, when idle it presents Apple's RPSystemBroadcastPickerView to begin a broadcast; when already sharing it calls stopShare(). It registers as a delegate observer and automatically keeps its icon and enabled state synchronized with the authoritative SDK share status via onUserShareStatusChanged. It continuously gates whether sharing is allowed (host share lock, multi-share setting, another user sharing, in-app share support) and disables itself when not.
behavior: The button reflects the authoritative share state reported by the SDK; its icon updates to the sharing state once a broadcast begins via onUserShareStatusChanged. The button does not override didMoveToWindow(); initial state is set at construction and thereafter updated by onUserShareStatusChanged.

cases.meaning: Local user is NOT sharing out; tapping starts a share

cases.name: stop
cases.meaning: Local user IS sharing out; tapping stops the share

typeDefinitions.note: Case names describe the ACTION the tap performs, not the current activity. currentType defaults to .stop at the property level but is overwritten in init() before display.

prerequisites: Zoom Video SDK initialized and registered with the toolkit via ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize(videoSDK:bundleId:) BEFORE constructing the button.

bundleId passed to initialize should be the ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension bundle identifier; it is assigned to RPSystemBroadcastPickerView.preferredExtension so the picker pre-selects your extension. If empty, preferredExtension is left unset and the user must pick manually.
Host app must provide a configured ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension and entitlements; this button only presents the system picker, it does not implement the extension.
Construct and use on the main thread (@MainActor).
lifecycle.ifNotInitialized: If ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDK is nil, the button constructs in the 'start' state, is DISABLED (canCurrentUserStartScreenShare() returns false when the share helper is nil), and tap actions take no effect (callback guards on the share helper being non-nil).

actions: build descriptor (40x40, clear bg, secondaryLabel icon color, zero padding, iconname StartShare/StopShare)

exitPoints.note: Delegates are held weakly by CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate.

lifecycle.didMoveToWindow: This button does not override didMoveToWindow(). Initial state is set at construction and thereafter updated by onUserShareStatusChanged.
lifecycle.delegateModel: The button does NOT assign itself to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate. It registers with the toolkit fan-out delegate ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate (CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate), enabling multiple observers. Child delegates are stored weakly (NSHashTable.weakObjects()).

states.description: Local user is NOT sharing out

stateTransitions.action: guard canCurrentUserStartScreenShare(); if !shareHelper.isSharingOut(), remove any existing picker by tag, add RPSystemBroadcastPickerView (tag 10001, showsMicrophoneButton=false, preferredExtension=bundleId if non-empty), then send .allTouchEvents to its internal UIButton to trigger it
stateTransitions.to: unchanged (transition to .stop happens later via onUserShareStatusChanged(.start/.resume))
stateTransitions.condition: no SDK return value to inspect because starting is driven by the system picker; icon updates to the sharing state once the broadcast begins
authoritative; only when changed user == getMySelf()
authoritative; only when changed user == getMySelf()

postCallbackEffect: After every onUserShareStatusChanged for the local user, isEnabled is recomputed via canCurrentUserStartScreenShare(), regardless of which status branch was taken (including the default/no-icon-change branch).

appliedAt: top of tap callback (short-circuits action if false)

apis.name: init
apis.description: Reads shareHelper.isScreenSharingOut() to choose initial state/icon, constructs the button, sets isEnabled from canCurrentUserStartScreenShare(), and registers as a delegate observer.

apis.name: init(coder:)
apis.description: NOT SUPPORTED. Calls fatalError. Do not instantiate from Storyboard/XIB.

apis.name: setStartShareIcon
apis.description: Overrides the icon used for the 'start' state. Applied immediately if currently in the start state.
sideEffects: Updates startIcon; calls switchTo(.start) if currentType == .start

apis.name: setStopShareIcon
apis.description: Overrides the icon used for the 'stop' state. Applied immediately if currently in the stop state.
sideEffects: Updates stopIcon; calls switchTo(.stop) if currentType == .stop

apis.name: canCurrentUserStartScreenShare
apis.description: Returns whether the local user is currently permitted to start an in-app screen share, based on in-app-share support, host share lock, multi-share setting, and whether another user is sharing. Drives isEnabled and gates the tap action. Returns false defensively when the share helper is nil.
apis.returns: Bool (true if sharing may be started)

apis.name: switchTo
apis.description: Sets currentType and updates the displayed image to match (startIcon for .start, stopIcon for .stop). Internal; documented for completeness.
sideEffects: Sets currentType and the normal-state image

apis.name: dismissBroadcastPicker
apis.description: Removes the RPSystemBroadcastPickerView (located by tag kBroadcastPickerTag=10001) from the window if present. Called whenever the local user's share status changes (start, resume, none, stop) to clean up the transient picker view.
sideEffects: Removes the broadcast picker view from the window

inheritedConfiguration.warning: Do not use setIcon/setImage to represent share state; it is transient and overwritten on the next state change. Use the per-state setStartShareIcon / setStopShareIcon methods.

callbacks.name: onUserShareStatusChanged
callbacks.signature: public func onUserShareStatusChanged(_ helper: ZoomVideoSDKShareHelper?, user: ZoomVideoSDKUser?, shareAction: ZoomVideoSDKShareAction?)
callbacks.description: Fired when any user's share status changes. Filters to the local user (changed user must equal getSession()?.getMySelf()). Reads status via shareAction?.getShareStatus() (default .none). On .start/.resume -> switchTo(.stop) + dismissBroadcastPicker(); on .none/.stop -> switchTo(.start) + dismissBroadcastPicker(); other statuses -> no icon change. Afterwards isEnabled is recomputed from canCurrentUserStartScreenShare().
callbacks.stateChange: resyncs the icon to match SDK share status for local-user changes only; always re-evaluates isEnabled

statusHandling.default: no icon change (falls through); isEnabled still recomputed

noOpConditions: changed user is nil or not equal to the local user

errorHandling.strategy: Share starting is delegated to the OS ReplayKit broadcast picker. stopShare() returns a ZoomVideoSDKError, and .Errors_Success triggers the icon update to .start. The button reflects the authoritative share state reported by the SDK; its icon updates to the sharing state once a broadcast begins via onUserShareStatusChanged.

calls: (none) presents RPSystemBroadcastPickerView and programmatically triggers its UIButton
perAction.onSuccess: no immediate UI change; transition to .stop occurs on onUserShareStatusChanged(.start)
perAction.onResult: the icon updates to the sharing state once the broadcast begins via onUserShareStatusChanged. To respond to outcomes, observe SDK events via ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:).

errorHandling.retryStrategy: To respond to outcomes, observe SDK events via ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:) (e.g. implementing onFailed(toStartShare:user:) and on(inAppScreenShare:)).
recoveryActions: CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate forwards onFailed(toStartShare:user:) and on(inAppScreenShare:) to any observer that implements them

required: Initialize the toolkit (ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize(videoSDK:bundleId:)) before constructing the button.
Pass the ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension bundle id as bundleId so the picker pre-selects your extension.
Provide a configured ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension and entitlements in the host app; this button only presents the system picker.
Construct and use the button on the main thread.
forbidden: Instantiating via init?(coder:) / Interface Builder (traps with fatalError).
Assigning the button (or anything) directly to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate; use ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:).
Adding another view with tag 10001 (kBroadcastPickerTag) to the button's window; the button uses this tag to locate/dismiss the picker.
Using inherited setIcon/setImage to represent share state; it is overwritten on the next state change.
